messages:
Alex Chen: Heads-up team — Sales flagged a major customer ask: strict geo residency + graceful regional failover for inference. They want contract-level guarantees and a migration path. Need to scope for long-term roadmap (routing policies + multi-tenant isolation).
Maria Gomez: Can you paste the exact ask? is it full 'data never leaves region' or 'prefer region'?
Alex Chen: Quote from customer: 'All inference and KV cache must stay within EU unless we opt-in to cross-region failover; failover only to pre-authorized regions, with audit logs and SLAs.'
Jordan Lee: Product lean here — that language implies three things: region residency controls, per-tenant failover policy, and auditability/telemetry. Each has infra and contract implications.
Samir Patel: From infra POV: per-tenant region pins increase fragmentation and reduce bin-packing. If we do strict isolation we need dedicated capacity slices or strong soft-quota enforcement. Rough multiplier: ~2.0–2.5x overhead depending on headroom.
Nadia Ortiz: Phased approach suggestion: 1) region affinity + best-effort residency (low impact), 2) SLA-backed strict residency (paid tier with capacity reservation), 3) full air-gapped/private option.
Maria Gomez: Sales will push for strict SLA. They accept opt-in contracts but want clear fallback rules and notification. Also they want a short migration playbook for customers to move models/data.
Samir Patel: Operationally, fallback options: a) failover to pre-approved region using same model, b) failover to quantized/cheaper variant in another region, c) degrade to lower throughput with local queueing. Each has different cost/latency tradeoffs.
Jordan Lee: Launch criteria proposal (must have before GA):
- policy DSL to express tenant routing + fallback rules (example: `route.policy { region: eu; fallback: [eu, us]; quarantine: false }`)
- per-tenant telemetry + residency audit logs
- SLA language + opt-in contract templates
- migration tooling & docs (dry-run tooling + customer-facing checklist)
- infra capacity plan and cost model for reserved capacity
Maria Gomez: Add: end-to-end test plan with real customer prompt sets and quality guardrails for any model variant used in failover. Customers will reject silent quality regressions.
Samir Patel: Cost note: strict residency (reserved pools) => capacity planning + N+1 per region. We should include a 'soft-fallback' mode to limit worst-case spend while we negotiate contracts.
Nadia Ortiz: Telemetry owner volunteer: I'll own residency audit + routing metrics dashboard. Need an events schema for residency decisions.
Alex Chen: Ownership ask: Jordan -> policy DSL + migration; Samir -> infra capacity model + fallback mechanics; Maria -> SLA/contracts + customer comms; Nadia -> telemetry & tests. Agree?
Jordan Lee: Agree. I'll sketch DSL and a minimal OpenAPI for policy config by EOW.
Samir Patel: Agree. I'll run a capacity sensitivity model and two scenarios (strict reserved vs affinity) by next Tuesday.
Maria Gomez: I'll draft SLA options and fallback wording. Ask: can we propose a pilot for a single named customer in Q3? They want timeline.
Alex Chen: Proposal: Q3 pilot (limited customers, controlled failovers) -> Q4 GA for paid tier. If legal/compliance demands air-gapped, route to Private offering (longer timeline).
Maria Gomez: Sales will try to lock pilot for Q3, but we should set expectation: firm GA requires infra + SLA signoff.
deploy-bot: Canary scheduled: `geo-routing-v1` -> eu-west1 @ 1715010000 (internal canary only) :rocket:
Samir Patel: One more tech option: use prefix/KV caching to reduce cross-region state transfers. If we can keep KV local and only route stateless requests cross-region, that helps the residency story for low-latency inference.
Nadia Ortiz: We'll need eval datasets to verify quality parity for quantized variants if used in fallback. I'll coordinate with Applied ML.
Alex Chen: Next steps: Jordan to open PRD skeleton in #product-docs, Samir to attach cost scenarios, Maria to prep contract options. We'll reconvene next Tue to sign off pilot candidates. Thanks. :thumbsup:
